title: Permian · before the dinosaurs
description: The Permian is the last period of the Paleozoic. Dinosaurs had not yet evolved. It ended with the largest mass extinction in Earth's history, wiping out about 90% of all species.
majorEvents: Mass extinction · formation of Pangea · first reptiles

title: Early Triassic · dawn of dinosaurs
description: Life slowly recovered from the Permian extinction. The first dinosaurs appeared about 245 million years ago. Early forms like Eoraptor and Herrerasaurus roamed the supercontinent Pangea.

title: Middle Triassic · diversification
description: Dinosaurs began to diversify alongside other reptiles. The climate was hot and dry. Small theropods and early sauropodomorphs appeared.

title: Late Triassic · dominance begins
description: Dinosaurs became the dominant land vertebrates. The Triassic ended with another mass extinction that cleared the way for dinosaurs to rule the Jurassic.

title: Early Jurassic · giants arise
description: The Jurassic period saw the rise of giant sauropods and the first birds. Pangea began to split apart. The climate was warm and humid.

title: Middle Jurassic · age of giants
description: Sauropods reached enormous sizes. The first stegosaurs appeared. The supercontinent continued to break apart.

title: Late Jurassic · golden age
description: The peak of Jurassic dinosaur diversity. Large theropods like Allosaurus hunted giant sauropods. The first birds evolved.

title: Early Cretaceous · new species
description: Flowering plants appeared. New dinosaur species evolved, including early raptors and ceratopsians. The continents continued to separate.
majorEvents: Flowering plants appear · new dinosaur species

title: Late Cretaceous · the end
description: The last and most diverse period of dinosaur evolution. T. rex, Triceratops, and Spinosaurus ruled. An asteroid impact 66 million years ago ended the dinosaur era.
